questions.prompt: What is the key difference between speed and velocity?
options: Speed is always larger than velocity
Speed is a scalar; velocity is a vector
Velocity is the rate of change of speed
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar (magnitude only). Velocity is a vector — it has both magnitude AND direction. A car going 60 km/h north has velocity 60 km/h north; a car going 60 km/h south has the same speed but opposite velocity.

questions.prompt: A car travels 120 km in 2 hours, going from A to B (a straight road). What is the average velocity?
options: 60 km/h in the direction from A to B
240 km/h in the direction from A to B
Cannot be determined without more information
questions.explanation: Average velocity = displacement / time = 120 km from A to B divided by 2 h = 60 km/h in the direction from A to B. Direction is part of the answer because velocity is a vector.

questions.prompt: A particle's instantaneous velocity at time t is defined as:
options: Total displacement divided by total time
The limit of average velocity as the time interval approaches zero
The slope of the acceleration-time graph at t
The total distance divided by total time
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity v(t) = lim(Δt→0) Δx/Δt = dx/dt. Graphically it is the slope of the position-time curve at that instant. Option (a) is average velocity, and (d) is average speed.
